mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary easing supports risk asset demand.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in < 55% of instances during FEDFUNDS decline periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS exceeding 5.0% for 3 consecutive months signals restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates weakening consumer demand for housing despite labor market strength, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Joint signal of declining HOUST and rising PAYEMS fails to predict negative returns when SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized) during early expansion phases supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during GDPC1 > 2.0% periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in < 55% of UNRATE decline periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: UNRATE exceeding 5.0% for 3 months indicates labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of UNRATE > 5.0% periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Rising FEDFUNDS combined with declining industrial production (INDPRO) indicates monetary tightening suppressing economic activity, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and falling INDPRO fails to predict negative returns when SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) above 110.0 during early expansion phases signals manufacturing growth supporting corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
regime_hint: early expansion phase of industrial activity
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during INDPRO > 110.0 periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.
